module purpose: A collection of bus fabrics: a switch that arbitrates between local masters (ports A/B) and forwards the chosen request to an external bus (x_req_o) and returns responses; a gateway that decodes request addresses to per-port requests and aggregates device responses; optional request/response register stage; and AMO/RVS units that implement atomic read-modify-write and reservation semantics with timeout monitoring.

use-case flows.value: Issue of a selected master request on the external bus (assemble x_req_o fields and assert x_req_o.stb)
Arbitration and hold/release sequencing (state machine keeps S_IDLE / S_BUSY_A / S_BUSY_B and latches/clears a_req/b_req)
Forward external responses back to the selected master (data copied; ack/err gated by the grant decision)
Address decode and per-port request generation (gateway: compute port_sel from req_i.addr and produce port_req(i))
Aggregate device responses into int_rsp and drive external rsp_o (data copy; ack/err ORed; keeper.err influences ack/err)
Request-monitoring and timeout (keeper): detect start of request, count cycles, set err on timeout and clear on response or lock change
AMO RMW sequence and compute: schedule read, capture rdata, compute alu_res, and drive write (sys_req_o.data) during write phase
Reservation (RVS) flow: compute rvso, control request forwarding for RVS, set sc_fail on store-conditional failure, and encode sc result into core response
Reset to known values (clear arbiter/switch/gateway registers and keeper state under rstn_i)

conceptual assets.concept: Arbitration/grant decision (which master is granted and when a request is driven)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The switch's behavior depends on the stored state and the computed selection that decide which master supplies x_req_o and when the strobe is asserted. Evidence in the RTL: the state register is clocked into the FSM (state occurrence 3, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 55) and the FSM computes sel/stb (sel SELECTED_BY state at sel occurrence 4, line 87; stb SELECTED_BY state at stb occurrence 5, line 115). sel then gates the external request fields (GATED_BY sel records on x_req_o fields at lines 140–147) and the internal strobe is copied to the external strobe (COPIES stb -> x_req_o.stb at line 158). Corruption of state/sel/stb would change which request is presented or when it is presented, directly violating the implemented forwarding decision (lines 83–131, 140–158).

conceptual assets.concept: Master lock state (per-master lock bits that hold a granted transfer until the master releases the lock)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The switch captures lock inputs and uses them to hold and release grants: locked bits are stored and used in the busy-state arms to gate the strobe and to decide when to return to S_IDLE. RTL evidence: locked is reset and clocked (locked occurrence 3, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 57) and locked_nxt is derived from the masters' lock inputs (locked_nxt DERIVES_FROM a_req_i.lock / b_req_i.lock at locked_nxt occurrence 4, line 111). The busy-state branches test locked(0)/locked(1) and use that to hold stb or to release when the master's lock clears (lines 88–103). Integrity of these lock bits is required for the module to preserve the intended lock/atomic behaviour.

conceptual assets.concept: Address decode result (which gateway port a request is routed to)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The gateway decides which device port receives a request by comparing req_i.addr with configured base addresses and enabling per-port requests. RTL evidence: port_sel bits are produced by address comparisons (port_sel(0) <= '1' when A_EN and (req_i.addr(31 downto a_lo_c) = A_BASE(31 downto a_lo_c)) at line 356), and port_req(i) is then driven and its .stb masked by port_sel in the request process (lines 372–379). The port_sel signal is therefore the structural reference of the decode decision (port_sel occurrence 2, GATED_BY req_i.addr at line 356). Integrity of port_sel is required so the request is routed to the correct target.

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregated device response (int_rsp) that the gateway presents to the system output
conceptual assets.reasoning: Device responses are OR-combined into int_rsp and then drive rsp_o: the response process builds tmp_v from enabled port_rsp(i) values and assigns int_rsp <= tmp_v (line 395). The RTL then copies int_rsp.data to rsp_o.data (line 399) and gates ack/err with keeper.err (lines 400–401). Map evidence: int_rsp is derived from port_rsp (int_rsp occurrence 2, DERIVES_FROM port_rsp at line 395) and is copied to rsp_o.data (line 399). Integrity of int_rsp is therefore required so the module's external response reflects the combined device responses as implemented.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway request-tracking and timeout state (keeper.busy, keeper.cnt, keeper.err, keeper.halt, keeper.lock)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The gateway monitors an outstanding request (keeper.busy) and increments a timeout counter; on timeout it sets keeper.err and clears busy, and keeper.err is ORed into rsp_o. RTL evidence: bus_monitor initializes and updates keeper fields on reset and clock (keeper.busy CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 419) and increments keeper.cnt (line 422) and sets keeper.err when the counter saturates (lines 423–425). keeper.err is then used in response outputs (rsp_o.ack / rsp_o.err gating at lines 400–401). Corrupting keeper state would change timeout detection and the gateway's reported ack/err behavior (lines 414–427 and 399–401).

conceptual assets.concept: AMO RMW execution context and result (arbiter state / wdata/rdata/cmd and alu_res) that produce write-back data and core responses
conceptual assets.reasoning: The AMO RMW unit sequences a read, computes a result and issues the write. RTL evidence: the arbiter record (fields cmd, rdata, wdata and state) is clocked and controls the sequence (arbiter whole CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 763); alu_res is clocked and computed from arbiter.rdata/wdata/cmd (alu_res CLOCKED_BY clk_i at line 839 and computed in process amo_alu lines 833–846). sys_req_o.data is gated to alu_res in write states (sys_req_o.data <= alu_res when arbiter.state = S_WRITE at line 813). The core response also depends on arbiter.rdata (core_rsp_o.data takes arbiter.rdata or sys_rsp_i.data depending on arbiter.state at line 826). Integrity of arbiter fields and alu_res is therefore established by these RTL flows.

conceptual assets.concept: Reservation/SC result and control (rvso and sc_fail) used to implement RVS semantics and to encode SC failure into core responses
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RVS unit computes a reservation indicator (rvso) from AMO fields and uses it when deciding whether to forward or gate requests; sc_fail is set on a failed store-conditional and alters the core response. RTL evidence: rvso is computed from core_req_i.amo/amoop (rvso GATED_BY core_req_i.amo/core_req_i.amoop at rvso occurrence 4, line 935) and sc_fail is clocked and set on the RVS failure condition (sc_fail CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 957 and sc_fail assignment at line 957). sc_fail is ORed into core response data/ack (core_rsp_o.ack and core_rsp_o.data at lines 963–964). Integrity of rvso/sc_fail is therefore required for correct RVS behavior and correct encoding of store-conditional results.
